articles.zh: 为什么一开口说英语就慌
body: Plenty of learners can read a newspaper in English and still freeze the moment someone asks them a question out loud. The problem is rarely grammar. It is the fear of being judged while the words are still forming.
很多人能看懂英文报纸，可一被人当面问话就僵住。问题基本不在语法，而在于话还没组织好，就已经怕被人笑话了。
Teachers call this language anxiety. Your heart speeds up, your mind goes blank, and words you have known for years suddenly vanish. It is a physical reaction, not proof that you are bad at English.
老师把这叫「语言焦虑」。心跳加快、大脑空白，学了好几年的词突然就想不起来了。这是身体的应激反应，不能证明你英语差。

The way out is not more textbooks but more low-stakes practice. Talk to yourself while cooking, record a thirty-second voice note, or speak with one patient friend. Treat mistakes as data, not disasters.
解法不是再多买几本书，而是多做「压力小」的练习：做饭时自言自语、录一段三十秒语音、或者只跟一个有耐心的朋友聊。把错误当数据，别当灾难。

articles.zh: 社交媒体是不是已经死了
body: Social media was built so that friends could see each other's lives. Open any app today and you mostly see strangers, adverts and clips chosen by an algorithm. The 'social' part has quietly shrunk.
社交媒体当初是为了让朋友之间看见彼此的生活。可今天随便打开一个软件，刷到的多半是陌生人、广告和算法挑的片段。「社交」这部分已经悄悄缩水了。
AI has sped this up. Machines now write posts, generate faces and even reply in the comments, so users are less sure whether a real person is on the other side of the screen.
AI 让这个过程更快了。机器能写文案、生成人脸，甚至替人回评论，于是用户越来越不确定屏幕那头到底是不是个真人。

Some people are drifting back to small group chats and newsletters, where the audience is smaller but real. Perhaps social media is not dying, only splitting into a loud public square and a quiet living room.
有些人正退回到小群聊和邮件订阅里——受众更少，但都是真人。也许社交媒体没有死，只是分裂成了一个吵闹的广场，和一个安静的客厅。
tips: 公共广场（比喻公开的舆论场）

articles.zh: 英国人嘴上说的，和心里想的
body: British politeness can be confusing for learners. When a colleague says 'that's an interesting idea', they may not be praising you at all. Very often they mean the opposite and are being gentle about it.
英式礼貌对学习者来说很容易看走眼。同事说「这个想法很有意思」，可能根本不是在夸你，多半是委婉地表达相反的意思。
Phrases like 'I'll bear it in mind' or 'with the greatest respect' work as soft padding. They protect the listener's feelings while still delivering a no, and everyone local understands the code.
像「我会记在心上」「恕我直言」这样的说法，其实是一层软垫子。它们既保住了对方的面子，又把「不行」说了出来，本地人都懂这套暗号。
You do not have to copy this style, but recognising it saves you from awkward misunderstandings. Listen to tone and context, not only to the dictionary meaning of each word.
你不一定要学这种说话方式，但听得懂能帮你少踩坑。多听语气和上下文，别只盯着每个词的字典意思。
tips: 把某事记在心上（常用于委婉推脱）
恕我直言（后面往往接反对意见）
缓冲的软垫（比喻委婉说法）

articles.zh: 讨厌的食物，也能吃出感情
body: Almost everyone has a food they refuse to touch. Coriander, blue cheese, bitter melon. Some of that dislike is written into our genes, but a surprising amount of it is simply habit.
几乎每个人都有一样打死不碰的食物：香菜、蓝纹奶酪、苦瓜。这种讨厌有一部分写在基因里，但很大一部分其实只是习惯。
Researchers say taste can be retrained. Trying a disliked food in tiny amounts, ten or more times, often turns disgust into tolerance and sometimes even into pleasure.
研究者说味觉是可以重新训练的。把讨厌的食物每次只吃一点点、吃上十来回，反感往往会变成能接受，有时甚至真的喜欢上了。
Context matters too. The same vegetable feels different when a friend cooks it well, or when you eat it abroad on a good day. Memory seasons food as much as salt does.
环境也很关键。同一样菜，朋友做得好吃、或者你在国外心情不错时吃到，感觉就完全不同。记忆给食物调味，一点不比盐少。

articles.zh: 减肥药，真的一劳永逸吗
body: New weight loss injections have become headline news around the world. They work mainly by slowing digestion and telling the brain that the body is already full, so people simply eat less.
新型减肥针在全世界都上了头条。它们主要靠减慢消化、并告诉大脑「已经饱了」来起作用，于是人自然就吃得少了。
Doctors warn that they are medicine, not magic. Side effects can include nausea and loss of muscle, and for many patients the weight returns once the injections stop.
医生提醒：这是药，不是魔法。副作用可能包括恶心和肌肉流失，而且不少人一停针，体重就回来了。
There is also a bigger question. If a drug can quiet our appetite, what does that say about the food environment that made us so hungry in the first place?
还有一个更大的问题：如果一支药就能压住食欲，那当初把我们的胃口撑这么大的那个饮食环境，又该怎么说呢？
